direct_answer:
Aker BP states that it conducted (and in 2024 revised) a double materiality assessment (DMA) aligned with CSRD/ESRS, covering both (i) impact materiality (impacts from its activities on environment and society) and (ii) financial materiality (financial risks and opportunities sustainability issues pose to its business model and performance, including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources) [Source 1][Source 3]. The DMA included mapping impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs), their dependencies, and their connection to Aker BP’s own operations and value chain; it considered activities, business relationships and geographies, with focus in own operations on oil and gas production, in the upstream value chain on development projects/construction activity, and it also notes downstream impacts related to use of petroleum products [Source 3].

Methodologically, Aker BP describes a structured, iterative process: defining business context (activities, business model, value chain, stakeholders, boundaries), identifying actual and potential IROs using top-down and bottom-up approaches with internal/external stakeholder input and quantitative sources, assessing and prioritising IROs based on impact and financial materiality criteria using a standardized rating system, and validating outcomes by management and the Board with ongoing monitoring/updates [Source 4]. It applies IRO assessments using “severity x likelihood” (similar to consequence x probability in enterprise risk management), uses company scales aligned to its enterprise risk management matrix, documents assessments in the same tool as other company risks, and gives “special attention” to dependencies between impacts and related risks/opportunities [Source 1].

Stakeholder engagement is described as being incorporated into the DMA via open and proactive dialogue and multiple channels; in 2024 this included in-depth interviews and workshops with internal management and subject matter experts, and the 2024 process was based on interviews performed in the previous year involving owners, key suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 2]. Aker BP also cites public consultation processes for impact assessments required for all delivered PDOs (with “over 40 key stakeholders” receiving reports) and a whistleblowing channel as additional avenues for stakeholder input/concerns [Source 2]. The Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) and Executive Management Team (EMT) are kept informed about affected-stakeholder views through channels including the DMA approval process and integrity-channel case reporting [Source 1].

Sustainability matters identified as material from both an impact and a financial perspective (i.e., high impact and high financial relevance / “strategic and highest priority”) are: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use and circular economy [Source 2].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide a clear description of the DMA’s double-materiality scope (inside-out and outside-in), an outline of the process steps, integration with enterprise risk management (severity x likelihood), consideration of value chain, and stakeholder engagement channels [Source 1][Source 2][Source 3][Source 4]. The report also explicitly identifies which topics are high on both impact and financial materiality (climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, resource use and circular economy) [Source 2]. However, the retrieved evidence does not fully specify the qualitative/quantitative thresholds used to determine materiality, nor does it provide the complete list of material matters/IROs from both perspectives beyond the matrix caption, limiting full ESRS 1 alignment based solely on the provided excerpts [Source 1][Source 4].
disclosure_gaps: Specific qualitative and/or quantitative thresholds (and cut-offs) used to determine when an impact/risk/opportunity and a sustainability matter becomes material (beyond stating severity x likelihood and a standardized rating system) [Source 1][Source 4].

A complete, explicit list of sustainability matters that are material on both dimensions beyond the matrix caption (e.g., confirmation for all ESRS topics/sub-topics and entity-specific matters) [Source 2].

Detailed explanation of how impact materiality severity dimensions (scale, scope, irremediable character) are operationalised in the DMA (not evidenced in the retrieved passages) [Source 1][Source 4].
Detailed explanation of how financial materiality magnitude is assessed and how likelihood/magnitude thresholds are applied (only general statements provided) [Source 1][Source 6].

Explicit description of interdependencies between impact and financial materiality outcomes for each material topic (only general statement that special attention is given to dependencies) [Source 1].
key_findings: DMA covers both impact materiality (inside-out) and financial materiality (outside-in), including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources [Source 1].

Assessment maps IROs, their dependencies, and links to own operations and value chain; considers activities, business relationships and geographies; focuses own-operations assessment on oil and gas production and upstream value chain on development projects, and notes downstream impacts from product use [Source 3].

Process is described as structured and iterative: define context/boundaries and stakeholders; identify IROs using top-down and bottom-up approaches with stakeholder input and quantitative sources; assess/prioritise using standardized ratings; validate by management/Board; monitor and update [Source 4].

IRO assessments use severity x likelihood and are aligned with enterprise risk management scales/matrix; assessments are documented and prioritised in the same tool as other company risks, with attention to dependencies between impacts and related risks/opportunities [Source 1].

Stakeholder engagement informs the DMA through dialogue and channels including PDO impact-assessment public consultations (over 40 stakeholders), whistleblowing, and interviews with owners, suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities; ARC/EMT are kept informed through DMA approval and integrity-channel reporting [Source 1][Source 2].

Topics identified as material from both impact and financial perspectives (strategic/highest priority) are: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use and circular economy [Source 2].
